content.text:
I checked the brief line by line against the 8-K Exhibit 99.1.

**Headline findings**

- No figure in the brief is wrong. Every number I could tie back to the release (revenue, net income, operating pre-tax income, both gross margins, segment lines, guidance, cash/debt, dividends) matches on figure, period and basis.
- Three key facts are missing rather than wrong, and two of the gaps are the kind an IC would notice:
  - **GAAP diluted EPS ($2.27, down 2%)** is never given. The brief substitutes GAAP net income ($2.2B, down 1%) — correct in itself, but it leaves the headline GAAP-vs-operating EPS spread ($2.27 vs $2.93) unquantified.
  - **Operating pre-tax income margin (19.2%, up 0.3 pts)** is absent. The brief gives operating pre-tax income in dollars (+3%) and both gross margins, so the one margin line that expanded is the one omitted.
  - **Q2 free cash flow ($2.5B, down $0.3B YoY)** is absent. The brief reports operating cash flow of $2.6B, *up* $0.9B, in its place. Directionally this reads as a cash-flow tailwind when the FCF line — the measure management guides to — declined. Given the brief repeats the full-year "+$1 billion FCF" guidance, the missing in-quarter FCF decline is the most consequential omission.
- On guidance, the brief carries the 4–5% constant currency growth range but drops the release's note that, at current FX rates, **currency is expected to be neutral to growth** for the year. I scored the fact as stated correctly since the figure, period and basis are right, but flagging the omission.
- Minor wording: the release says IBM will invest "**more than** $10 billion" in quantum over five years; the brief says "$10 billion."

facts.evidence: GAAP revenue from continuing operations was $17.2 billion, up 1% year-over-year
Operating (non-GAAP) diluted EPS was $2.93, up 5% year-over-year.
Software revenue was $7.8 billion, up 5% year-over-year
The company now expects full-year 2026 constant currency revenue growth in the range of 4–5%.
Full-year 2026 free cash flow is expected to increase by about $1 billion year-over-year.
The company returned $1.6 billion to shareholders in dividends during the second quarter.
Infrastructure revenue was $3.8 billion, down 7% year-over-year, with Distributed Infrastructure up 37% and IBM Z down 42%.
